claims.text: A 7.1-magnitude earthquake struck Kumamoto, Japan, causing widespread damage, injuries, and structural collapses.
A shopping mall collapsed and the outer walls of Kumamoto Castle were damaged during the earthquake.
Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi pledged a full government response to the earthquake.
An earthquake with a preliminary magnitude of 6.8 struck Kumamoto prefecture on southern Kyushu island, Japan, late Tuesday afternoon.
The US Geological Survey initially estimated the Kumamoto earthquake magnitude at 7.1 before revising it to 6.8.
Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi stated: "Power outages and fires have occurred in some areas, and there has also been damage to roads and bridges and the collapse of buildings."
An explosion occurred inside an Aeon shopping mall in Kumamoto shortly after the earthquake, trapping people inside.
The disaster management agency instructed approximately 300,000 people to move to evacuation centres following the earthquake.
The Japan Meteorological Agency reported over 60 aftershocks ranging in magnitude from 1 to 4 following the main tremor.
A tsunami warning issued immediately after the earthquake was lifted within two hours.
A series of powerful earthquakes in Kumamoto in 2016 killed 277 people either directly or from disaster-related injuries.
Over 40,000 households in Kumamoto Prefecture were experiencing power outages as of 01:30am local time.
The Aeon mall in Kumamoto had reopened on June 13, 2026, following extensive rebuilding after the 2016 earthquake.
Mall staff helped evacuate about 200 visitors outside before an explosion destroyed the walls and structure of the Aeon mall.
The earthquake struck Kumamoto prefecture on Kyushu island at 16:27 local time (07:27 GMT) on Tuesday.
Two workers were found in cardiac arrest and nine others were reported missing after a chimney collapsed at Nippon Paper's Yatsushiro Plant.
Wildfires burning near Bordeaux are threatening vineyards across France's largest wine region amid severe drought and high temperatures.
Chateau Palmer director general Thomas Duroux stated: "What we are experiencing this year is a wake-up call. We are facing something we have never seen before."
The Bordeaux fine wine market has lost nearly 20 percent of its value over the past five years according to the Liv-ex Bordeaux 500 Index.
A wildfire in southwestern France damaged parts of Biscarrosse's commercial district.
Wildfires across the Spanish countryside have forced tens of thousands of people to evacuate their homes.
Madrid regional leader Isabel Díaz Ayuso described the wildfires as "the biggest natural catastrophe in the history of Spain."
Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez declared areas affected by wildfires to be official disaster zones.
More than 56,500 people have been evacuated from the Madrid region since the wildfires started.
Spanish Minister for Ecological Transition Sara Aagesen reported that around 77,000 hectares have been affected by wildfires across Spain.
Nearly 4,000 people were evacuated from tourist campsites and villages around Lacanau west of Bordeaux due to advancing wildfires.
French President Emmanuel Macron stated that the current wildfire situation is the toughest crisis France has dealt with since World War II.
A wildfire in Ávila, west of Madrid, became the largest in Spain's recorded history after burning 50,000 hectares.
Wildfires across France, Spain, and Italy have forced the evacuation of approximately 330,000 people over a single week.
US President Donald Trump and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu met at the White House for a nearly 90-minute closed-door discussion on Tuesday.
White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt stated that the meeting between Donald Trump and Benjamin Netanyahu was "positive and productive."
Donald Trump publicly criticized Benjamin Netanyahu during an interview on Fox & Friends for leaking planned talking points about Iran's Pickaxe Mountain facility.
Demonstrators gathered outside the White House to protest Benjamin Netanyahu's visit to Washington.
Donald Trump stated regarding Iran's nuclear infrastructure: "We took out their nuclear site, and we'll have to take out Pickaxe if we don't make a deal."
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy held brief closed-door talks with Donald Trump at the White House prior to Trump's meeting with Netanyahu.
Donald Trump publicly confirmed a heated June phone call in which he referred to Benjamin Netanyahu using crude profanity.
Benjamin Netanyahu and Volodymyr Zelenskyy traveled to Washington to attend a Capitol memorial service for the late Republican Senator Lindsey Graham.
Benjamin Netanyahu faces an upcoming Israeli national election in late October as well as an ongoing trial for corruption.
Oman submitted a proposal to Iran to manage the Strait of Hormuz using a voluntary fee structure backed by regional nations.
Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi stated that Tehran rejected an Omani proposal for an equal division of transit lanes in the Strait of Hormuz.
Prior to the US-Israel military action on February 28, the Strait of Hormuz carried one-fifth of global energy supplies.
Foreign ministers of the Gulf Cooperation Council held a video conference on Tuesday to discuss maritime navigation security.
The Omani maritime navigation proposal is modeled after the Strait of Malacca system where ships voluntarily contribute to fund safety and environmental care.
Iran's joint military command rejected Donald Trump's proposal to pay damages to commercial vessels using frozen Iranian assets.
Yemen's Houthi forces declared a blockade on Saudi Red Sea ports on July 20 and later claimed to fire ballistic missiles at a Saudi oil tanker.
US President Donald Trump paused a 13-night campaign of airstrikes against Iranian targets following recommendations from military commanders.
Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baqaei stated: "At present we are not engaged in any negotiations with the United States."
Donald Trump told Axios: "We are in very deep talks with Iran. If they don't work out, we will go back to very strong military action."
Cockroach Janta Party volunteer Junaid Malik filed a petition with the Supreme Court alleging unlawful detention and police harassment.
A internal CRPF review concluded that Rapid Action Force personnel followed standard operating procedures when using pellet guns during July 20 anti-NEET protests.
During the July 20 protest clashes in New Delhi, 47 Rapid Action Force personnel and between 3 and 5 protesters were injured.
The Lok Sabha opened debate on the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026.
Congress MP Gaurav Gogoi called the anti-paper leak bill a "cosmetic exercise" that reflected the government's admission of failure.
Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigned on July 25 following sustained youth demonstrations led by the Cockroach Janta Party.
At least 22 students in India have committed suicide this year due to scandals surrounding competitive examination paper leaks.
Congress MP Shashi Tharoor urged Parliament to overhaul the examination framework from single high-stakes tests to continuous testing to prevent paper leaks.
Shashi Tharoor stated in the Lok Sabha that student suicides in India increased from 8,000 in 2014 to 14,600 currently.
The Forward Seamen's Union of India reported that 13 Indian seafarers among 15 crew members are trapped aboard the vessel MV AMIR1 at the Ukrainian port of Chornomorsk.
Two Indian crew members went missing after jumping overboard when the cargo ship AGN RAGNAR was attacked by drones near the Danube river outlet on July 25.
Indian Shipping Minister Sarbananda Sonowal instructed officials during a high-level review meeting to prevent Indian seafarers from being caught in geopolitical conflicts.
The Indian Ministry of External Affairs summoned Ukrainian Ambassador Oleksandr Polishchuk to protest repeated Black Sea strikes on commercial ships carrying Indian crews.
Chief Officer Sagar Gupta was killed during a July 18 attack on the merchant vessel MV OMORFI.
Four Indian nationals were killed and one was critically injured in a July 19 strike on the MV Golden Leo near Odesa.
External affairs ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal stated that six Indian vessels carrying 125 Indian seafarers are stationed west of the Strait of Hormuz.
India represents the second-largest community of seafarers worldwide, comprising 12.16 percent of the global maritime workforce with over 320,000 professionals.
Recent monsoon flooding in Assam caused seven additional deaths over a 24-hour period, leaving over 300,000 people affected.
Assam Assembly Speaker Ranjeet Kumar Dass, Deputy Speaker Habbey Teron, and most Assam state legislators pledged one month's salary to flood relief.
The All Assam Students' Union sent a letter to Prime Minister Narendra Modi requesting that Assam's flood and erosion problem be classified as a national problem.
Monsoon floods in Assam have caused 75 deaths and displaced more than 7.5 lakh people.
The Odisha state government initiated evacuation operations in low-lying areas as floods affected over 100,000 residents across four northern districts.

Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma announced an additional ex-gratia payment of ₹5 lakh from the CM's Relief Fund to families of flood victims, raising total ex-gratia to ₹9 lakh per deceased person.
The Assam government allocated an interim cash relief of ₹15,000 per family for approximately 100,000 severely affected households in Sivasagar, Charaideo, Jorhat, and Golaghat districts.
